articles.title: Another Trump meme coin contest promises an ‘exclusive’ dinner with the president
articles.summary: The firm behind President Donald Trump’s crypto keepsake known as a meme coin is promoting yet another contest for investors to secure an invitation to “the...
articles.body:
The firm behind President Donald Trump's meme coin is promoting yet another contest for investors to secure an invitation to "the most exclusive dinner in the world" — a sequel to the May 2025 gala that experts called a textbook pay-to-play scandal.

The meme coin's website on Thursday offered "an evening with 3 Legends and President Donald J. Trump" at his private club in Washington , DC , for the top 185 holders of the $TRUMP coin. The top 29 purchasers of the crypto keepsake will be invited to a VIP reception "with YOUR FAVORITE PRESIDENT," and the top four will receive an 18-karat Trump-branded gold watch.

The contest began Wednesday and runs through November 12, according to the site.

At the same time, the site also states that "no attendees will be granted a private meet & greet with the President" and that "no gifts will be accepted." The event is scheduled for November 22.

Early Thursday afternoon, the GetTrumpMemes.co site appeared to crash.

It's the latest episode of Trump and his businesses seemingly profiting off his presidency. Financial disclosures have shown him raking in more than a billion dollars off his crypto ventures and making thousands of stock trades , including in companies that are directly affected by his policies. The White House has repeatedly said Trump is not involved in his investment accounts and that his portfolio "is independently managed by third-party financial institutions."

And it's not the first meme coin event the president has held. The top 220 holders of the $TRUMP meme coin were invited to a black-tie dinner at Trump's golf club outside Washington, DC, in May 2025, with those in the room having contributed millions in investment in his crypto token. The 25 biggest investors also got access to a small VIP reception with the president.

The White House referred questions about the event to the hosts. The companies behind the event, CIC Digital and Fight Fight Fight LLC, are affiliates of the Trump Organization, which didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump has made more than $1 billion from his crypto portfolio, most of which he launched shortly before retaking office in January 2025. Investors in those products have been less fortunate: A report from the watchdog Public Citizen recently tallied investors had racked up $4.7 billion in paper losses on Trump crypto assets managed by the president's adult sons.

Memecoins are particularly risky investments because they have no intrinsic value and are prone to sudden collapses. The US Securities and Exchange Commission last year wrote that memecoins have a failure rate "exceeding 90% for new tokens."

Trump launched his memecoin shortly before his inauguration in 2025. Its value initially surged to $70 but quickly fell. It currently trades around $2.

articles.title: Crypto thieves attacked man in home and threatened to kill pregnant wife's baby in 'horrific' robbery
articles.summary: The man was beaten with hammers until he transferred hundreds of thousands of pounds of cryptocurrency.
articles.body:
Warning: This story contains distressing details

A businessman was beaten with hammers by masked men who broke into his home and threatened to kill his heavily pregnant wife unless he transferred hundreds of thousands of pounds of cryptocurrency.

Speaking to the BBC, the couple, who want to remain anonymous, described the attack as "horrific" and said they feared for their unborn baby's life.

The attackers left in a car driven by a getaway driver after the man transferred his crypto savings.

Crimestoppers are offering a £10,000 reward for information in the attack, which was captured on home security footage and is being investigated by the police.

Experts say it is one of a growing type of violent theft known as a "wrench attack" targeting cryptocurrency investors.

As crypto coins have risen in value, reports of these violent robberies linked to digital assets have emerged in the UK, France and the US.

Once funds are transferred, recovering them can be extremely difficult.

The man, who the BBC is calling James, said three intruders forced their way into their Solihull home before launching an assault which lasted 45 minutes.

"The door gets pushed open, I can see gloves coming in, balaclavas," he said.

James tried to fight the men off but they hit him in the face, head and ribs with hammers.

His wife, who was seven months pregnant, was held down on the sofa by one of the criminals.

"He's got a pillow over her face," James said. "He's literally suffocating her on the sofa. I can hear her screaming, 'I can't breathe'."

The couple still had no idea what the criminals wanted until one of the men demanded James unlock his phone and hand it over.

James said the attackers appeared to know he owned cryptocurrency, but had little understanding of how to access it.

Instead, they were taking instructions from someone else connected via a live video call.

"I can hear the guy on FaceTime saying: 'Show me everything on his phone. Show me what apps he's got'," he said.

When the caller identified a crypto wallet containing substantial funds, the threats escalated dramatically.

"He was basically saying: 'Look, if you don't send us this money now, we're going to stab your wife in the stomach and kill your baby. We're going to kill your wife'," James said.

His wife, who also did not want to be named, described the attack that happened in December last year as "horrific" and said she feared James had been killed when he was unresponsive on the floor.

The woman, in her early thirties, was expecting her third child at the time and said she feared she might lose the baby due to the stress of the attack. The baby survived and was born at full term.

The men left after James transferred his savings - hundreds of thousands of pounds of cryptocurrency - to the digital wallet of the man on the video call.

They also stole several luxury Rolex watches.

James said before they left, he heard the man on the video call tell his accomplices: "You can have 10 grand each but I am taking the rest."

Unlike money held in a conventional bank account, cryptocurrency is often controlled directly by the owner through digital wallets or physical storage devices.

For criminals, that combination of speed, anonymity and irreversibility can make crypto holders attractive targets.

Whilst the vast majority of cryptocurrency theft happens online through hacks and scams, crypto investigators at Chainalysis say "wrench attacks" have surged in recent years.

According to their research, $30m (£22.6m) had been stolen so far this year up to June in violent robberies, making 2026 likely to become the single-worst year for violent crypto attacks on record. Home invasions are also on the rise this year, it found.

The US, Brazil, and Thailand are hotspots but France has seen the largest number of attacks by far, as a result of a data breach at a tax office that has apparently allowed wealthy crypto holders to be located.

"The physical security assumptions that protect traditional wealth, such as bank vaults and armored cars, do not automatically apply in crypto. Often, holders keep their assets in comparatively low security setups, like self-custody wallets, that can be compromised without any institutional gatekeeper standing in the way," said researchers in their report.

James said he became an amateur investor in crypto coins in 2020 and made enough money to quit his job in 2023 to trade full time.

Now he has lost everything and is looking to get back to his traditional job.

Police have yet to identify the attackers.

Crimestoppers is offering a £10,000 reward for information leading to progress in the investigation.

Alan Edwards from the charity hopes people might have information about the three attackers, the driver who was parked outside without a face covering, or the man on the phone.

"These criminals are obviously serious and part of some kind of organised crime gang," he said.

"People might be scared to give us information but we are independent of the police and keep people completely anonymous."

The three attackers are all thought to be in their late teens or early 20s and one of them was a black male with a scar under his left eyebrow.

James said he has little hope of recovering the stolen funds, but instead wanted to see those responsible brought to justice.

He also wants his experience to serve as a warning.

"They threatened my wife and my baby," he said. "People need to understand these risks are real."

articles.title: The Lakers have named their new public address announcer
articles.summary: The Lakers have officially named the successor to Lawrence Tanter, their longtime public address announcer who passed away last week.
articles.body:
For over 40 years, Lawrence Tanter made his mark on the history of the Los Angeles Lakers as their public address announcer at home games, first at The Forum in Inglewood, Calif., and later at Staples Center/Crypto.com Arena. His tenure began during the 1982-83 season and spanned the Showtime era, the Kobe Bryant era and LeBron James' tenure with the franchise.

Tanter missed several games late last season due to a stroke and retired shortly afterward. Last week, it was announced that he had passed away .

The Lakers have now named their official public address announcer for this season. His name is Derrin Horton, and he commented on his new gig, per Benjamin Royer of the Southern California News Group .

"It's a dream," Horton said Thursday, speaking with local media for the first time since taking over for Tanter. "I mean, are you kidding me? The Lakers? … "When I heard about LT and the opportunity here, I reached out and I had a chance to communicate with LT. He was such a legend, and I considered him to be a friend. So now to be here, obviously, there's no way you can fill his shoes, and so you just come here with a passion and a goal to be informative and entertaining and be a part of 'Showtime'."

"It's a dream," Horton said Thursday, speaking with local media for the first time since taking over for Tanter. "I mean, are you kidding me? The Lakers? …

"When I heard about LT and the opportunity here, I reached out and I had a chance to communicate with LT. He was such a legend, and I considered him to be a friend. So now to be here, obviously, there's no way you can fill his shoes, and so you just come here with a passion and a goal to be informative and entertaining and be a part of 'Showtime'."

Horton has worked for over 35 years as an anchor, reporter, host, play-by-play announcer and voice actor. Residents of the Los Angeles area may know Horton as an anchor at KTLA and KCAL, two local television stations. He has also worked for NFL Network.

According to Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times , Horton started out his audition for his new role with the Lakers by trying to imitate Tanter's one-of-a-kind delivery.

"Horton showed up to his audition and instinctively tried to emulate Tanter's signature baritone voice," Nhi Nguyen wrote. "He wanted to sound like what he thought the classic PA announcers should sound like. Lakers president and chief business officer Lon Rosen stopped the tryout in mid-sentence. "'He said, "Hey! Knock it off! I want to hear your voice,"' Horton said. 'And so I just was myself.'"

articles.title: Ledger wallet tampering suspected after reports of crypto thefts
articles.summary: A spy implant in some Ledger crypto wallets may be the root of an $86 million supply chain attack.
articles.body: Reports have been mounting that users of the Ledger crypto wallet have seen their accounts drained, and it appears to be related to tampered hardware sold by CryptoBillis. Ledger has asked CryptoBillis to pause all sales of its wallets while it conducts an investigation. Ledger has confirmed that “one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant.” Photos and videos posted on X and Threads appear to show a small circuit board sandwiched under the screen. The implant allegedly intercepts anything displayed on the screen, including the seed passphrase shown during the initial setup. Using an embedded SIM card, the implant then sends that information back to the attacker, who can then siphon funds from user accounts. [Media: Reports indicate that whoever is behind the hack has stolen over $86 million worth of crypto from hundreds of wallets. There’s no indication that Ledger’s systems have been compromised or that wallets purchased directly from the company have been affected. Instead, the issue appears to be a supply chain attack primarily involving users in Southeast Asia and the CryptoBillis reseller. Ledger has provided guidance on how to check if your wallet has been tampered with. Update October 10th, 2026: Added additional statment from Ledger.

articles.title: ‘We’ll kill you’: How a late-night cab ride turned into a 15-minute ordeal for Mumbai student
articles.summary: Juhu police arrest 3 within 12 hours for allegedly kidnapping an 18-year-old student in an Uber cab and robbing Rs 14,250 in Mumbai.
articles.body: MUMBAI: An 18-year-old first-year university student has accused three men of kidnapping him in an aggregator cab, driving him around Juhu for 15 minutes, threatening him with a knife and extorting Rs 14,250 before he was let go early on Oct 10.Juhu police registered a case of kidnapping, extortion and robbery against history-sheeters Azad Maniyar (34), Dipesh Chavan (29) and Mondaya Devendra alias Kishan (30) who allegedly forced PA Agarwal into the cab, stole Rs 5,250 from his pocket and compelled him to transfer Rs 9,000 through an e-wallet. They allegedly made Agarwal call his sister before transferring money through UPI.Police caught the three accused at their hideouts in Andheri within 12 hours of the incident involving Agarwal at 1.30 am on Oct 10. “The accused allegedly forced Agarwal into a cab he had booked to return to his PG accommodation, assaulted the driver, forced him inside and sped away. The trio were tracked through technical analysis using the phone number through which money was credited from Agarwal’s account to an e-wallet. Agarwal had earlier gone to drop his aunt’s daughter and her three friends after they had dinner on Oct 9,” said a police officer of the Juhu police station.According to Agarwal’s complaint, three unidentified men allegedly assaulted an Uber driver and forced Agarwal to remain in the car after he dropped his aunt’s daughter and her three friends at a girls’ hostel in Vile Parle (West) around 1.30 am. Agarwal said one man opened the driver’s door, slapped him and questioned where the passengers had come from. The man allegedly told Agarwal there had been a rape at a girls’ hostel in Yenda the previous day and claimed they were union members. Agarwal, who said he was frightened, remained in the car. One of the men, identified by a companion as Azad, allegedly instructed the Uber driver where to drive and took Agarwal around Juhu and other areas. His two companions followed the car on a scooter, the FIR said.Police said Maniyar allegedly threatened Agarwal with a knife near Juhu Ruia Park and forced him to transfer Rs 5,000 to a UPI account. Two accomplices, who had followed them on a scooter, allegedly restrained Agarwal while Maniyar took Rs 5,250 from his trouser pocket. “The group later allegedly forced Agarwal to obtain money from his sister and transfer another Rs 4,000 to the same account. They allegedly threatened to kill him if he disclosed the incident before releasing him near Mithibai College. Agarwal contacted friends and went to lodge a complaint. articles.title: Binance.US Seeks $100 Million to Expand Its Crypto Business
articles.summary: Binance.US is looking to raise as much as $100 million as the crypto exchange seeks to beef up its US business amid intensifying competition for digital-asse...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Binance.US is looking to raise as much as $100 million as the crypto exchange seeks to beef up its US business amid intensifying competition for digital-asset customers.

The company is targeting a valuation of about $1 billion in the private round, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified discussing confidential information.

World Liberty Financial, co-founded by President Donald Trump among others, was among those made aware of the fundraising, according to people familiar with the matter. Another person familiar with the situation said the Trump family's crypto venture isn't participating. The size and valuation of the fundraising, along with the makeup of its investors, could change as the process continues.

Spokespeople for Binance.US and World Liberty declined to comment.

Launched in 2019, Binance.US operates separately from the global Binance exchange, though Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao is a large shareholder of both entities. Binance.US raised more than $200 million in 2022 at a $4.5 billion pre-money valuation.

The latter lost much of its market share following Binance Holdings Ltd.'s 2023 settlement with US authorities and is now seeking to regain ground against larger rivals. The exchange has also explored expanding into new businesses, including prediction markets, Bloomberg News previously reported.

The fundraising bid comes as digital-asset companies seek to capitalize on a more favorable US regulatory environment. Established exchanges are adding products while offshore rivals pursue a larger presence in the country.

Binance.US has discussed the possibility of tapping external sources of trading liquidity, potentially including Binance's international exchange, according to a person familiar with the matter. No approach has been decided, the person said.

Binance.US is also looking to restore some of its state money-transmitting licenses as part of its broader US expansion efforts, according to a person familiar with the matter.

World Liberty already has ties to the global Binance exchange, which holds a lion's share of its USD1 stablecoin, according to the crypto tracker Arkham. The token was also used by an investment firm tied to leaders of the United Arab Emirates to fund its purchase of a $2 billion stake in Binance.

articles.title: Strategy stock falls as Michael Saylor's bitcoin giant faces index-level threat
articles.summary: Strategy stock fell more than 3% on Friday after index provider MSCI announced new eligibility rules that could lead to the removal of Michael Saylor's bitco...
articles.body:
Strategy ( MSTR ) stock fell 8% on Friday after index provider MSCI announced new eligibility rules that could lead to the removal of Michael Saylor's bitcoin juggernaut from its global stock indexes.

MSCI said Thursday it will adopt new rules to exclude certain "non-operating companies" from its indexes, including those whose primary business resembles that of an investment fund rather than a traditional operating company.

Exclusion could include Strategy, the world's largest corporate holder of bitcoin, along with other digital asset treasury companies. Such an action is expected to force index-tracking funds to sell shares of affected companies.

MSCI said it will publish a final list of affected companies on Nov. 11, with the new rules taking effect after the market closes on Nov. 30.

Strategy, led by executive chair Saylor, had previously criticized the proposal as discriminatory against digital asset treasury companies. The company currently holds about 4% of bitcoin's total supply.

On the other hand, Fundstrat head of digital asset strategy Sean Farrell doesn't see Strategy's potential elimination from the index as a significant worry.

"I still think the market can absorb the associated flows," Farrell wrote late Thursday to clients, estimating that selling across MSCI-linked products amounts to "around $2 billion."

"The market has had months to prepare for this outcome. Strategy itself issued more than $2 billion of common stock in August," Farrell added.

Bitcoin's price ( BTC ) fell slightly Friday morning.

articles.title: The Crypto Cop Who Took Down a Global Scam Network from Brooklyn
articles.summary: Crypto scams cost Americans more than $11 billion last year. A Brooklyn prosecutor found a way to hit the networks behind them.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- By the time Alona Katz hurried home from her office in downtown Brooklyn late on Oct. 6, the trap was already set. After months of planning, the chief of Brooklyn's crypto fraud unit was about to orchestrate one of the most sweeping international crackdowns a local prosecutors' office had ever attempted.

The operation, which took place across three time zones, was the culmination of a chase Katz had begun almost as soon as she was appointed chief of Brooklyn District Attorney's Virtual Currency Unit three years ago.

If things went according to plan, Katz would shut down a computer crime network run out of Eastern Europe that had been victimizing Brooklyn residents and had stolen tens of millions of dollars.

The tension grew as the countdown began to start the operation.

"We couldn't entirely control what happened next," Katz said.

At 2 a.m., dozens of computer servers that Katz's team had targeted started going down. She would get no sleep that night.

As crypto use has become more widespread, the global crypto fraud economy has exploded in size. In 2025, reported US losses from cryptocurrency fraud reached $11.4 billion, roughly triple from three years earlier, according to the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

This new frontier of fraud has flummoxed traditional law enforcement agencies, particularly at the local level. Before the Brooklyn DA opened the VCU office, victims who sought help from the New York Police Department were often told to go elsewhere because the NYPD didn't understand the scams, Eric Gonzalez, the Brooklyn District Attorney, said in an interview.

"They would say, 'Go to civil court.' Sometimes they would say, 'Call the FBI, because we don't have the ability to help here because it's an international scam.'"

Federal prosecutors weren't much help either. Most of the fraud targeting citizens in Brooklyn ranges from hundreds to tens of thousands of dollars, significant for the victims but too small to be of interest to the federal authorities, who largely only look into scams of six- or seven-figure dollar amounts, Gonzalez said.

An NYPD spokesperson said its Financial Crimes Task Force investigates cryptocurrency crimes and pointed to a recent case in which the department helped bust a $3.5 million crypto scam. An FBI spokesperson said the agency seeks to prevent crypto fraud through community outreach and working with the private sector.The Black Sheep

articles.title: Bitcoin Rebounds Above $82,000 as Oil's Retreat Lifts Risk Mood
articles.summary: Bitcoin popped back above $82,000 on Monday, rebounding with risk assets as oil prices declined.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) popped back above $82,000 on Monday, rebounding with risk assets as oil prices declined.

The original cryptocurrency climbed as much as 2.3% in early Asia trading and was hovering around $82,400 at noon in Singapore. Smaller tokens also advanced. Ether was up as much as 3.7%, while Solana gained more than 4.6%.

Cryptocurrencies have joined a tentative recovery in risk appetite after oil retreated from a five-month high on signs that supplies from the Middle East have held up since the US war with Iran broke out. Brent crude fell as much as 2%, while a gauge of S&P 500 futures was up roughly 0.8% and Nasdaq 100 futures were up 1.3%.

Improving macro conditions have helped Bitcoin reverse its trend from last week, when it fell roughly 3% along with a selloff in stocks led by technology shares amid renewed doubts about massive spending on artificial intelligence.

Today's move higher is a "retracement after a big risk-off week," said Damien Loh, chief investment officer at Ericsenz Capital.

"No news is good news," he said. "I don't see any near-term drivers for it to break new highs, and I think the risk is for the downside given overall risk environment."

Oil remains elevated at roughly $107 a barrel, higher than prices for most of last week.

Institutional demand has also pulled back from Bitcoin for two consecutive weeks. US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded $228.6 million in outflows last week following $681 million in outflows the previous week.

Bitcoin remains within last week's trading range of $80,000 to $85,000.

articles.title: JPMorgan Asset Sees Bitcoin Beating Stocks, But With a Catch
articles.summary: JPMorgan Asset Management has included Bitcoin in its long-term capital market assumptions for the first time, forecasting returns that could beat stocks, bo...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- JPMorgan Asset Management has included Bitcoin in its long-term capital market assumptions for the first time, forecasting returns that could beat stocks, bonds and gold in a milestone for its Wall Street acceptance.

But there's a catch: Bitcoin's extreme volatility threatens to undermine its appeal on a risk-adjusted basis.

JPMorgan's base case projects annualized returns of 10% over the next decade, but also assumes annual volatility of 55%, more than three times that of US large-cap stocks. The firm stops short of incorporating Bitcoin into its main portfolio models, it said in a report this week, citing its unstable correlations with other assets.

Such volatility can eat into compounded returns as steep losses require even larger gains to recover. That's a risk familiar to Bitcoin ETF investors who bought near the cryptocurrency's peak of just over $126,000 in 2025, only to see their holdings lose as much as 50% as prices retreated.

"We believe it is premature to consider BTC as a diversifier in a balanced portfolio," the JPMorgan team including Tim Lintern, Thushka Maharaj and Sean Daly wrote. "But should volatility continue to decline and correlations to other asset stabilize, this may evolve in the future, particularly as regulation becomes clearer and liquidity and price discovery continue to improve."

Since the pandemic, various Wall Street firms have been making more earnest inroads into the world of cryptocurrencies, shifting from cautious inquiry to more meaningful experimentation that's included making the trading of certain coins available for clients, putting out crypto-focused funds and dabbling with tokenization, among other things.

The JPMorgan analysts say that even as many investors see Bitcoin as a speculative asset, they're still exploring cryptocurrencies — a tenth of clients recently surveyed said their portfolios held crypto, and roughly 17% said they planned to "prioritize crypto." That's thanks, in part, to a regulatory framework that has become more developed and better defined.

Still, Bitcoin right now doesn't cut it as a diversifier in balance portfolios due to its "unstable correlations" to other assets, the bank's researchers said. "If correlations stabilize and volatility declines, BTC's portfolio utility may improve in the future," they wrote.

articles.title: Wall Street brings blockchain into the fold
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS — The buzz at Money 20/20 is focused on consumers being on the verge of near-instant banking transfers, including at night or on weekends, Axios' R...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS — The buzz at Money 20/20 is focused on consumers being on the verge of near-instant banking transfers, including at night or on weekends, Axios' Ryan Lawler and Lucinda Shen report.

Why it matters: America's financial giants have talked for years about bringing blockchain — the technology that cryptocurrencies like bitcoin are built on — into their systems. Now they're actually doing it.

That shift to instant transfers could also make investing faster and more convenient: Digital versions of stocks could let investors transfer shares around the clock, even when exchanges are closed.

"It's becoming more mainstream institutionally than it ever has been," Digital Currency Group investor Aaron Fu tells Axios, pointing to financial institutions building more blockchain infrastructure in-house.

💡 How it works: Financial institutions have begun using private blockchains to instantly track money and investments as they change hands.

Yes, but: Using the technology behind cryptocurrencies doesn't necessarily mean using the currencies themselves.

Banks can create digital versions of the dollars customers already have on deposit.

💰 State of play: Money 20/20 attendees say that the conversation has moved from "Is this possible?" (the answer is yes) to figuring out exactly how banks will put these services into the electronic hands of consumers like you and me.

The industry group that handles much of the recordkeeping and settlement behind U.S. stock trades is preparing a service that creates digital tokens representing securities held in its system. This is called "tokenization."

Already, Citibank has said its tokenized-deposit service operates in seven markets, letting clients move funds between Citi accounts on a private blockchain.

🔎 Reality check: Competing tokenization efforts could create different versions of the same asset trading on separate networks.

That could confuse investors, reduce liquidity, and make it harder to establish reliable prices.

The bottom line: Blockchain is closer than ever to revolutionizing banking. First, banks, brokers and asset managers must connect systems so consumers and investors can move assets between them as easily as within them.
